results.title: Expressions built from one, addition and multiplication
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: An expression is either the constant $1$, or a sum $e_1 + e_2$ of two expressions, or a product $e_1 \times e_2$ of two expressions. Expressions are formal syntax trees, so the tree structure plays the role of parentheses.

results.title: Value of an expression
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The value of an expression is the natural number obtained by evaluating it: the constant $1$ has value $1$, the value of $e_1 + e_2$ is the sum of the values of $e_1$ and $e_2$, and the value of $e_1 \times e_2$ is the product of their values.

results.title: Number of ones in an expression
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of ones of an expression is the number of occurrences of the constant $1$ in it: the constant $1$ has one, and both $e_1 + e_2$ and $e_1 \times e_2$ have as many as $e_1$ and $e_2$ together.

results.title: Achievable numbers of ones

results.title: Integer complexity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The integer complexity of a positive integer $n$ is the least number of ones in an expression whose value is $n$, that is, the least number of ones needed to write $n$ using $1$, $+$, $\times$ and parentheses.

results.title: Expressions bound the integer complexity from above

results.title: Integer complexity of a sum

results.title: Integer complexity of a product

results.title: Integer complexity extended to all natural numbers

results.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequence of functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$. The sequence is locally uniformly bounded on $U$ when every $x \in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$ and a real $C \ge 0$ such that $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in V$.

results.title: A uniformly bounded sequence on an open set is locally uniformly bounded
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open, let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and let $C \ge 0$ be real. If $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in U$, then $(F_n)$ is locally uniformly bounded on $U$.

results.title: Locally uniformly bounded sequences are uniformly bounded on compact subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is locally uniformly bounded on $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Then for every compact set $K \subseteq U$ there is a real $C \ge 0$ with $|F_n(y)| \le C$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $y \in K$.

results.title: Montel's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $U \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ be open and let $(F_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, each holomorphic on $U$, that is locally uniformly bounded on $U$. Then there are a strictly increasing map $\varphi : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, holomorphic on $U$, such that $F_{\varphi(n)} \to f$ locally uniformly on $U$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Binomial point mass with success probability one half
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Gaussian approximation to the symmetric binomial point mass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Gaussian (local CLT) approximation to `binomProbHalf n k`, `√(2/(π n)) · exp(-(k - n/2)² / (n/2))`.

results.title: Lattice index in the local De Moivre–Laplace theorem
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The integer index `k = ⌊n/2 + x·√n/2⌋` corresponding to the parameter `x` in the local DeMoivre–Laplace statement: it picks the lattice point near `n/2 + x √n / 2`, so that `(2k - n)/√n ≈ x`.

results.title: The De Moivre–Laplace index tends to infinity
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The index `localDMLIndex x n` tends to infinity as `n → ∞`, for any fixed `x : ℝ`.

results.title: The complementary De Moivre–Laplace index tends to infinity
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The complementary index `n - localDMLIndex x n` also tends to infinity, so both `k` and `n - k` are eventually arbitrarily large.

results.title: The De Moivre–Laplace index over n tends to one half
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The ratio `localDMLIndex x n / n` tends to `1/2` as `n → ∞`, because the correction `x √n / 2` is `o(n)`.

results.title: Factorial in terms of the Stirling sequence
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Rewriting of `m!` in terms of Mathlib's `Stirling.stirlingSeq`: `m! = stirlingSeq(m) · √(2m) · (m/e)^m`.

results.title: Stirling decomposition of the binomial-to-Gaussian ratio
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Algebraic rewriting of the ratio `binomProbHalf n k / gaussianApproxHalf n k` using Stirling's formula, separating it into a Stirling-sequence factor, a square-root factor, a power-of-`n` factor, and an exponential correction.

results.title: Cubic bound on the symmetric entropy residual
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Third-order Taylor bound for the symmetric entropy expansion: `|(1+u) log(1+u) + (1-u) log(1-u) - u²| ≤ 6 |u|³` whenever `|u| < 1/2`. Used to control the deviation of the binomial coefficient from its Gaussian approximation.

results.title: Deviation bound for the De Moivre–Laplace index
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Eventually, the deviation `|2k - n|` for `k = localDMLIndex x n` is at most `|x| √n + 2`, since `k = ⌊n/2 + x √n / 2⌋`.

results.title: Logarithm of the binomial power factor
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Identity rewriting the logarithm of the power factor `nⁿ / (kᵏ (n-k)^{n-k} 2ⁿ)` plus the Gaussian exponent `(k - n/2)² / (n/2)` as `-(n/2) · ((1+u) log(1+u) + (1-u) log(1-u) - u²)`, where `u = (2k - n)/n`. This combines the log-binomial expansion with the Gaussian correction.

results.title: Binomial point mass is equivalent to a fixed Gaussian value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any binomial success-index sequence whose standardized displacement converges to `x`, the point mass is equivalent to the Gaussian expression evaluated at the fixed limit `x`. The number of trials may follow any natural-valued sequence tending to infinity.

results.title: Local limit theorem for the simple random walk
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The source's random-walk local limit theorem: every integer displacement sequence with `2 kₙ / √(2n) → x` has point mass equivalent to `(√(π n))⁻¹ exp(-x²/2)`. The scaling hypothesis itself implies that `n + kₙ` is a valid success index eventually.

results.title: Standardized displacement of the rounded index converges
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The rounded success index has standardized displacement converging to `x`.

results.title: The corrected binomial power factor tends to one
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: The product of the power factor `nⁿ / (kᵏ (n-k)^{n-k} 2ⁿ)` with the Gaussian correction `exp((k - n/2)² / (n/2))`, evaluated at `k = localDMLIndex x n`, tends to `1` as `n → ∞`. This is the key analytic estimate behind the local DeMoivre–Laplace limit theorem.

results.title: The complementary index over n tends to one half
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Companion to `localDMLIndex_ratio_half`: the ratio `(n - k) / n` for `k = localDMLIndex x n` also tends to `1/2`.

results.title: Binomial point mass is equivalent to its Gaussian approximation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The binomial point mass and its Gaussian approximation are asymptotically equivalent along the sequence `k = localDMLIndex x n`: `binomProbHalf n k ~ gaussianApproxHalf n k` as `n → ∞`. Combines Stirling's formula with the power-factor and entropy estimates.

results.title: Local De Moivre–Laplace theorem for $p = 1/2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Canonical rounded-sequence corollary of the local De Moivre–Laplace theorem: for any `x ∈ ℝ`, the binomial point mass divided by its moving Gaussian approximation along `localDMLIndex x` tends to `1`. The arbitrary integer-displacement statement with the fixed Gaussian value at `x` is `local_deMoivreLaplace_half_of_tendsto`.

results.title: Matrix arithmetic circuit
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, r, n \in \mathbb{N}$, a matrix arithmetic circuit is an arithmetic circuit over $F$ whose inputs are indexed by the entries $(i, k)$ of an $m \times r$ matrix together with the entries $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix, and whose outputs are indexed by the entries $(i, j)$ of an $m \times n$ matrix.

results.title: Matrix input assignment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$, the input assignment of $(A, B)$ is the function on the entry positions $(i, k)$ of an $m \times r$ matrix together with the entry positions $(k, j)$ of an $r \times n$ matrix that sends $(i, k)$ to $A_{ik}$ and $(k, j)$ to $B_{kj}$. It supplies the inputs of a matrix arithmetic circuit.

results.title: Circuits that compute the matrix product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A circuit $c$ over a field $F$ whose inputs are the entries of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix computes matrix multiplication when, for all matrices $A \in F^{m \times r}$ and $B \in F^{r \times n}$ and all $i < m$, $j < n$, its output at $(i, j)$ on the entries of $A$ and $B$ equals $(AB)_{ij}$.

results.title: Outer-product matrix circuit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $F$ of scalars and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit is the matrix arithmetic circuit for an $m \times 1$ matrix times a $1 \times n$ matrix with exactly $mn$ gates: for $i < m$ and $j < n$, the gate for $(i, j)$ multiplies the input at entry $(i, 0)$ of the first matrix by the input at entry $(0, j)$ of the second, and the output at $(i, j)$ is that gate.

results.title: The outer-product matrix circuit computes the matrix product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ computes the product of an $m \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$ matrix.

results.title: Size of the outer-product matrix circuit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every type $F$ of scalars and all $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the outer-product matrix circuit over $F$ has exactly $mn$ gates.

results.title: Outputs of a matrix multiplication circuit are gates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be a circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix, where $r \ge 1$. Then for all $i < m$ and $j < n$, the output of $c$ at $(i, j)$ is one of its gates, not a constant or an input.

results.title: Lower bound for matrix multiplication circuits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $c$ be a circuit over $F$ that computes the product of an $m \times r$ matrix and an $r \times n$ matrix, where $r \ge 1$. Then $c$ has at least $mn$ gates.
